notes: Tsomgo Lake (12,400 ft) is on the JN Road (Gangtok→Nathula) under Gangtok district. Kupup PS 03592-256252 + Sherathang PS 03592-266218 are the two listed stations on https://gangtokdistrict.nic.in/policestation/ that lie on the JN Road axis between Tsomgo and Nathula — kept name only, phones left out of payload as 5-digit numbers without STD prefix on the gov page are ambiguous (likely Army-network extensions, not civilian dial). PAP (Protected Area Permit) required for foreigners; permit issued by Gangtok Tourism. No pharmacy, mechanic, or guesthouse on .nic.in page → null.

name: Gurudongmar Lake
source_label: Mangan District Administration — Directory (DM, SP, SDM Mangan) — high-altitude restricted-permit zone, no civilian infra

fields.rescue_contact: SP Mangan (North): 03592-234242; DM Mangan: 03592-234856; SDM Mangan: 03592-234204 — for any rescue coordination, route via Mangan HQ. Indian Army manages all infrastructure beyond Thangu/Chopta (no civilian phone published).

notes: Gurudongmar Lake (17,800 ft) is in Mangan district near the China border, fully under Indian Army control beyond Thangu. NO civilian police station, hospital, pharmacy, mechanic, guesthouse anywhere within ~145 km — the trek/road from Mangan→Chungthang→Lachen→Thangu→Gurudongmar is entirely Army-administered above Lachen. Mangan District Hospital (Pentok, listed on https://mangan.nic.in/public-utility-category/hospitals/, inaugurated 2025) is the only district-tier govt hospital, ~145 km via Lachen route. STNM Gangtok (~250 km, 8-10 hr drive) is the realist tertiary fallback. Inner Line Permit mandatory from Mangan SDM (03592-234204). Indian Army medical post at Chungthang/Lachen handles emergencies but no civilian phone published — never fabricate Army contact. Helicopter evac is the only realistic rescue from Gurudongmar itself — coordinate via DM Mangan 03592-234856 and SP Mangan 03592-234242 (sources: https://mangan.nic.in/directory/, https://mangan.nic.in/office-superintendent-police/). All civilian fields → null. Honest-scarcity is the right answer here. October 2023 GLOF on South Lhonak Lake destroyed Chungthang dam + Sangkalan area; reconstruction ongoing — verify route status before trip.

name: Khangchendzonga National Park
source_label: Gyalshing District Administration — District Hospital + Sikkim Forest Dept (KNP UNESCO site, biosphere reserve, restricted permit)

fields.nearest_hospital: District Hospital Gyalshing (35 km via Yuksom road; in-park = no medical infra)
fields.rescue_contact: Geyzing PS: 8145887528 (PI Roshan Gurung); District Hospital Gyalshing: 03595-250634; KNP permits + park rescue coordination via Forest Environment & Wildlife Mgmt Dept, Sikkim (no published civilian emergency phone → use district admin)

notes: Khangchendzonga NP is a UNESCO World Heritage Site + biosphere reserve (1,784 sq km) — strict-permit zone managed by Sikkim Forest Dept. Yuksom is the trek-base village (Goecha La / Dzongri treks, 4-7 day trek). Inside the park there is NO civilian police station, hospital, pharmacy, mechanic, guesthouse — only forest department check-posts and trekker huts (Tshoka, Dzongri, Thansing, Lamuney). Mountain rescue is operator-managed (private trek companies) — no published .gov.in emergency phone for in-park rescue → null with honest-scarcity. For any in-park emergency, evac is multi-day trek back to Yuksom, then 35 km road to Gyalshing District Hospital (03595-250634, https://gyalshing.nic.in/public-utility/district-hospital-gyalshing/). Geyzing PS is the police touchpoint outside the park. KNP permits issued by Forest Dept Sikkim per https://www.sikkim.gov.in/departments/forest-environment-and-wildlife-department/wildlife. STNM Gangtok ~155 km via Pelling-Geyzing-Singtam (6-7 hr drive). All in-park civilian fields → null. This is the highest-risk emergency-scarcity dest in the state alongside Gurudongmar.
